title: 建築構造力学Ⅰ（再履修クラス）
subtitle: Structural Mechanics for Architecture I
teachers:
KAWAHARA Hiro
授業科目の学習・教育目標
educationalGoal: Students learn the mechanical characteristics of statically determinate beams, trusses, and frames, which are basic models of building structures. They understand the balance of forces that work on buildings and learn how to find reaction forces. Students understand the concept of resultant stress and the balance of free bodies, and learn how to determine the distribution of resultant stress in beams and frames. They learn how to find the axial forces in trusses by solving the nodal balance.
advice:
1. Building structures and structural mechanics
2. Equilibrium of force
3. Structure modeling and reaction forces
4. Loads and external forces
5. Mechanical classification of structures
6. Stress and resultant stress
7. Reaction forces and resultant stresses in statically determinate structures
8. Sectional properties
9. Material properties
10. Stress and member design
books:
Textbooks： Step up structural mechanics wrighten by Ota Kazuhiko
Reference books：None
Reserved books：None
requiredKnowledge:
Students must understand trigonometric functions and elementary mechanics.
A scientific calculator is required for testing.
Students should review the application of vector operations in Linear Algebra.

activityGoals.body: Building structure and loads/external forces can correspond to the dynamic model.
Students can determine the reaction forces of static structures.
Students can draw diagrams of axial force, shear force, and bending moment of a statically determinate structure
Students can explain the basic cross-sectional and mechanical properties of materials.
Students can determine the stress in a beam.

achievementLevels.ideal:
(1)	Students have acquired a basic knowledge of structural mechanics.
(2)	Students can describe the underlying formulas and find the exact solutions to those formulas.
(3)	Students can represent the resulting solutions graphically.
(4)	Students can show a simple structural model and can calculate stress.
(5)	Students can present a proposal to plan a rational building from a mechanical point of view for a simple building.
achievementLevels.standard:
(1)	Students have acquired a basic knowledge of structural mechanics.
(2)	Students can write the underlying formulas and understands the procedure for finding the solution.
(3)	Students can represent the resulting solution graphically.
